c.st: How to easily read 50 books a year

Trying to read a certain number of books is meaningless. Reading Proust’s Remembrance of Things Past is nothing like reading the latest 250-page blogpost-turned-popsci-selfhelp book.

Don’t worry about how many books you read. Just read good books you like.

c.st: How a nuclear attack on the U.S. might unfold, step by step
c.x: This article extends the faulty yet widely-accepted premise that only the US President can approve a nuclear strike. As the book "The Doomsday Machine - confessions of a nuclear war planner" by Daniel Ellsberg makes it plain, highly ranked officers (for example, the commander of Pacific Fleet) can issue a nuclear strike without approval from the President (or anyone else for that matter). This has been the case since Eisenhower's days.

c.st: Daniel Ellsberg Is Dying. and He Has Some Final Things to Say
c.x: I can recommend his sort of autobiographical books, Secrets and The Doomsday Machine. The former covers his time driving around in Vietnam with John Paul Vahn and his leaking of the Pentagon Papers, the latter covering nuclear planning and command and control. He had a number of top secret nuclear documents that he was planning on leaking that he buried in a landfill but were lost during a storm.

c.st: Consumer startups that said no to investor money
c.x:
Yeah I've read the high growth handbook as well.

Most VCs will not give up a seat, and most companies have absolutely no leverage.

The overwhelming majority of startups need funding to survive, this throws off the balance of control. The only startups that can dictate funding terms are the ones that have no real need to raise. Of course there are concessions, but relinquishing a board seat is not a common one.
